title.en: Home configuration recovery and rigid link invariants

summary: Verify that zero joint values recover the declared home transform and that each link keeps its rigid internal geometry as joints move.
objective: The zero configuration reproduces the home transform and each link keeps its rigid internal geometry as joints move.
applies_when: An articulated chain is driven by joint coordinates.
A home or zero configuration is declared.
A tool frame is displayed alongside the computed endpoint.
intent_signals: the arm stretches when I move the shoulder
check the zero pose of this arm
example_prompts: Check the forward kinematics conventions of this teaching arm.

principles: The zero joint vector must return the declared home transform; if it does not, the convention in the code differs from the documented one and every later pose is suspect.

Links are rigid, but consecutive joint-frame origins are not a rigid pair: a prismatic joint or a frame placed off the link changes that distance legitimately. Measure the distance between markers rigidly attached to the same link, and check declared joint displacement separately.
One transform convention is declared and used everywhere, because mixing conventions produces poses that look plausible in some configurations and wrong in others.
implementation: Evaluate the chain at the zero vector and compare the resulting end-effector transform with the declared home transform, reporting translation error as a length and rotation error as an angle with their own tolerances; a zero vector lying outside the operating limits is still a valid convention test.

Attach at least two markers to each link at fixed link-local offsets, sample at least a dozen joint vectors within limits, and record every within-link marker distance together with each declared joint displacement.
Compare the displayed tool frame with the computed end-effector frame and confirm that any visual tool offset is part of the declared model rather than an extra transform.
Recompute one sampled pose with an independently written implementation of the same convention and compare the results.
observable_checks: The zero configuration reproduces the home transform within the separate translation and rotation tolerances; a rotational mismatch of exactly a quarter turn suggests an axis convention difference rather than a numerical one.

Within-link marker distances are constant across all sampled configurations and each prismatic displacement matches its commanded value; a within-link distance that varies is a defect whose cause still has to be found, since transform order, a wrong joint axis and a mis-declared joint type all produce it.
The displayed tool and the computed endpoint coincide, and the transform convention is written down beside the result.

known_limits: Checks kinematic bookkeeping for an authored chain; it says nothing about payload, dynamics, collision avoidance or hardware calibration.
Authored verification guidance; no chain was evaluated or rendered for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt the scenario, scale and presentation to your subject; this record fixes what must be checked, not how the scene must look.

claims.statement: Forward kinematics finds the end-effector frame relative to a fixed frame from the vector of joint values, and the home configuration is the end-effector transform when all joint values are zero.
claims.scope: Open-chain rigid-link kinematics with declared joint axes and one documented convention.
